Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The Uí Ímair in Ireland had also suffered in 944 as Dublin was sacked that year by the High King of Ireland Congalach Cnogba, whose power base lay in Brega, north of Dublin on the lower reaches of the River Boyne. Amlaíb was allied with Congalach and may have gained power with his assistance.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Congalach and Amlaíb fought against Ruaidrí ua Canannáin, a rival for the _____ who belonged to the Cenél Conaill, based in modern County Donegal
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Congalach and Amlaíb fought against Ruaidrí ua Canannáin, a rival for the High Kingship who belonged to the Cenél Conaill, based in modern County Donegal.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: In 945 the two defeated part of Ruaidrí's army in _____ (modern County Louth) and the following year Amlaíb raided Kilcullen in the province of Leinster
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: In 945 the two defeated part of Ruaidrí's army in Conaille Muirtheimne (modern County Louth) and the following year Amlaíb raided Kilcullen in the province of Leinster.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: In 947 Ruaidrí routed _____ and Amlaíb at Slane
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Amlaíb was allied with Congalach and may have gained power with his assistance. Congalach and Amlaíb fought against Ruaidrí ua Canannáin, a rival for the High Kingship who belonged to the Cenél Conaill, based in modern County Donegal.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology

Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Blácaire was killed in 948 by _____, and was succeeded by Amlaíb's brother Gofraid
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: In 947 Ruaidrí routed Congalach and Amlaíb at Slane. Blácaire was killed in 948 by Congalach, and was succeeded by Amlaíb's brother Gofraid.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: If Erik did rule in _____ before Edmund's death, it was only for a short time
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: While Edmund certainly controlled Northumbria after Amlaíb was expelled and Ragnall killed, he may soon after have lost control of the north to a Scandinavian king named Eiríkr, usually identified with Eric Bloodaxe. If Erik did rule in Northumbria before Edmund's death, it was only for a short time.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Edmund was killed in 946, and succeeded by his brother _____
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Edmund was killed in 946, and succeeded by his brother Eadred. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records that Eadred "reduced all the land of Northumbria to his control; and the Scots granted him oaths that they would do all that he wanted".

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The following year, 949, by which time Blacáire was dead and Amlaíb's brother ruling in Dublin, the _____ invited Amlaíb to rule in York
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The Northumbrian submission to Eadred led to a meeting with the notables of York led by Archbishop Wulfstan in 947, but the following year King Erik was back ruling Northumbria and Eadred laid waste to the southern parts of the kingdom— Ripon is mentioned as a particular target—to force the Northumbrians to expel Erik, which they did. The following year, 949, by which time Blacáire was dead and Amlaíb's brother ruling in Dublin, the Northumbrians invited Amlaíb to rule in York.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: His return to _____ may have been with Eadred's agreement
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: His return to England may have been with Eadred's agreement.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: That year Máel Coluim mac _____, the king of Alba, raided Northumbria as far south as the River Tees, capturing many slaves and much loot
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: That year Máel Coluim mac Domnaill, the king of Alba, raided Northumbria as far south as the River Tees, capturing many slaves and much loot.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Whether this invasion was directed against Amlaíb, or perhaps intended to support him by plundering only northern _____ which may have been outside his control, is uncertain
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The following year, 949, by which time Blacáire was dead and Amlaíb's brother ruling in Dublin, the Northumbrians invited Amlaíb to rule in York. Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Again, whether this was aimed against Amlaíb, who was deposed in 952 and replaced by Erik, or was mounted against King Erik in support of Amlaíb, is unclear.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Erik's reign was short and the _____ kingdom of York was definitively incorporated into the kingdom of the English on his death in 954
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Erik's reign was short and the Viking kingdom of York was definitively incorporated into the kingdom of the English on his death in 954.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Amlaíb returned to _____, never again to rule in York
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Amlaíb returned to Ireland, never again to rule in York. The main beneficiary was the brother of Amlaíb's new wife Dúnflaith, Domnall ua Néill, who became the next High King of Ireland.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: This threat was perhaps what led to _____'s death in an ambush at Dún Ailinne (modern County Kildare) or at Tech Guigenn in the region of the River Liffey while collecting tribute in Leinster in 956
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Congalach's rival Ruaidrí was also dead, leaving Amlaíb's former ally as undisputed High King and thus a serious threat to Dublin and the south-eastern Irish kingdom of Leinster. This threat was perhaps what led to Congalach's death in an ambush at Dún Ailinne (modern County Kildare) or at Tech Guigenn in the region of the River Liffey while collecting tribute in Leinster in 956.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The main beneficiary was the brother of Amlaíb's new wife Dúnflaith, _____ ua Néill, who became the next High King of Ireland
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The main beneficiary was the brother of Amlaíb's new wife Dúnflaith, Domnall ua Néill, who became the next High King of Ireland.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The marriage linked Amlaíb not only to the northern Uí Néill kindred of Cenél nEógain, but also to the southern _____áin as he was now stepfather to Dúnflaith's young son Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The marriage linked Amlaíb not only to the northern Uí Néill kindred of Cenél nEógain, but also to the southern Clann Cholmáin as he was now stepfather to Dúnflaith's young son Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: In 960 the _____ of Ulster report that Cammán, son of Amlaíb mac Gofrith, was defeated at an unidentifiable place named Dub
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: In 960 the Annals of Ulster report that Cammán, son of Amlaíb mac Gofrith, was defeated at an unidentifiable place named Dub.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Sitriuc and his brothers appear to have raided _____ after this, but disappear from the record soon afterwards and do not appear to have returned to Ireland
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Sitriuc and his brothers appear to have raided Munster after this, but disappear from the record soon afterwards and do not appear to have returned to Ireland.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Amlaíb's activities in the early 960s seem largely to have been limited to occasional raids in _____
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Two years later one Sitriuc Cam—Cam means crooked or twisted and Cammán is simply the hypocoristic form of this byname, so that Sitriuc Cam and Cammán are presumed to be the same person—was defeated by the Dubliners led by Amlaíb Cuarán and the Leinstermen while raiding in Leinster. Amlaíb's activities in the early 960s seem largely to have been limited to occasional raids in Leinster.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Another raid south in 964 ended in a heavy defeat for Amlaíb near Inistogue (modern _____) at the hands of the Osraige
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Another raid south in 964 ended in a heavy defeat for Amlaíb near Inistogue (modern County Kildare) at the hands of the Osraige.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Having defeated these, in 968 he marched south and plundered _____, killing several notables, and laid siege to Dublin for two months
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: He attacked Kildare in 964, and it was a target again in 967 when Muiredach mac Faeláin, abbot of Kildare, a member of the Uí Dúnlainge kindred which ruled Leinster, was killed by Amlaíb and Cerball mac Lorcáin, a kinsman of Muiredach's. Until the late 960s Domnall ua Néill, Congalach's successor as would-be High King, was occupied with enemies close to home, and in Connacht and Munster, and did not intervene in Leinster or the hinterlands of Dublin.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Amlaíb, allied with the king of _____ mac Finn, retaliated by attacking the abbey of Kells in 969
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Amlaíb, allied with the king of Leinster Murchad mac Finn, retaliated by attacking the abbey of Kells in 969.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: A pursuit by ua Néill's allies was defeated near Ardmulchan (_____)
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: A pursuit by ua Néill's allies was defeated near Ardmulchan (County Meath).

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Domnall mac _____ was married to a daughter of Amlaíb, perhaps at about this time

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology

Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Domnall of Brega and Amlaíb fought against Domnall ua Néill's northern army at Kilmona in modern County Westmeath.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The battle at _____ did not end the war in the midlands
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Domnall of Brega and Amlaíb fought against Domnall ua Néill's northern army at Kilmona in modern County Westmeath. The battle at Kilmona did not end the war in the midlands.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: This campaign appears to have established _____ ua Néill as effective overlord of the midlands and Leinster for some years
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Domnall's army, which included allies from Ulaid, was defeated, and Ardgal mac Matudáin, king of Ulaid, and Cináed mac Crongilla, king of Conaille Muirtheimne, were among those killed. Monasterboice and Dunleer were burned after the battle and fighting spread to the lands of Clann Cholmáin the following year when Domnall ua Néill's enemies there drove him out, only for him to return with an army and ravage both Mide and the lands around Dublin before marching south to attack Leinster.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: In 977, in unknown circumstances, _____ ua Néill's sons Congalach and Muirchertach were killed and Amlaíb is given credit for their deaths by the annals
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Monasterboice and Dunleer were burned after the battle and fighting spread to the lands of Clann Cholmáin the following year when Domnall ua Néill's enemies there drove him out, only for him to return with an army and ravage both Mide and the lands around Dublin before marching south to attack Leinster. This campaign appears to have set up Domnall ua Néill as effective overlord of the midlands and Leinster for some years.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Domnall made no effort to avenge the deaths, retiring to the monastery at _____ where he died in 980
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Domnall made no effort to avenge the deaths, retiring to the monastery at Armagh where he died in 980.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The Dubliners campaigned against _____ the late 970s
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: This campaign appears to have set up Domnall ua Néill as effective overlord of the midlands and Leinster for some years. The Dubliners campaigned against Leinster the late 970s.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The overking of _____, Úgaire mac Túathail, was captured in 976
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The Dubliners campaigned against Leinster the late 970s. The overking of Leinster, Úgaire mac Túathail, was captured in 976.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: He was evidently ransomed or released as he was killed, along with _____ mac Riain of Uí Cheinnselaig of south Leinster, fighting against the Dubliners in 978 at Belan (County Kildare)
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: He was evidently ransomed or released as he was killed, along with Muiredach mac Riain of Uí Cheinnselaig of south Leinster, fighting against the Dubliners in 978 at Belan (County Kildare).

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Úgaire's successor _____ was little more fortunate, being captured by the Dubliners the following year
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Úgaire's successor Domnall Claen was little more fortunate, being captured by the Dubliners the following year.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Following the death of _____ ua Néill, Amlaíb's stepson Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill claimed the title
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Following the death of High King Domnall ua Néill, Amlaíb's stepson Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill claimed the title.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Máel _____ had become king of Mide and head of Clann Cholmáin in 975 and had inaugurated his reign with an attack on his stepfather when he burned "Thor's Wood" outside Dublin
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Following the death of High King Domnall ua Néill, Amlaíb's stepson Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill claimed the title. Amlaíb's former ally Domnall son of Congalach had died in 976, removing one potential rival, and as Amlaíb had killed two of Domnall ua Néill's sons he may have cleared the way for Máel Sechnaill to take power.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: In _____áel Sechnaill had the support of the Leinstermen when he faced Amlaíb's sons—Amlaíb himself was by now an old man—near the hill of Tara
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: In 980 Máel Sechnaill had the support of the Leinstermen when he faced Amlaíb's sons—Amlaíb himself was by now an old man—near the hill of Tara.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: The Dubliners too had allies as the Irish annals record the presence of warriors from the Isle of Man or the _____
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: The Dubliners too had allies as the Irish annals record the presence of warriors from the Isle of Man or the Hebrides.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Máel _____ occupied the city and imposed a heavy tribute on the citizens
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: In 980 Máel Sechnaill had the support of the Leinstermen when he faced Amlaíb's sons—Amlaíb himself was by now an old man—near the hill of Tara. Amlaíb's son Ragnall (Rögnvaldr) was among the dead in the battle which followed, and although several kings fighting alongside Máel Sechnaill were killed, the result was clearly a crushing blow for Dublin.

Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Amlaíb's son Ragnall (Rögnvaldr) was among the dead in the battle which followed, and although several kings fighting alongside Máel Sechnaill were killed, the result was clearly a crushing blow for Dublin. Máel Sechnaill occupied the city and imposed a heavy tribute on the citizens.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Among his wives was _____, daughter of Murchad mac Finn, King of Leinster, and future wife of Brian Boru
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Among his wives was Gormflaith, daughter of Murchad mac Finn, King of Leinster, and future wife of Brian Boru. Gormflaith's son Sitric Silkbeard was king of Dublin after Glúniairn's death.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Gormflaith's son _____ was king of Dublin after Glúniairn's death
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Gormflaith's son Sitric Silkbeard was king of Dublin after Glúniairn's death.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Amlaíb's other children included Gytha, who married _____, Máel Muire, who married Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill, and Harald, possibly the grandfather of Godred Crovan
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Amlaíb's other children included Gytha, who married Olaf Tryggvason, Máel Muire, who married Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill, and Harald, possibly the grandfather of Godred Crovan.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: It derives from the _____ word cúar meaning bent or crooked
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: It derives from the Old Irish word cúar meaning bent or crooked.

Amlaíb Cuarán.question: It is first applied to him in the report of the battle of Slane in _____ in the Annals of Ulster
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: It is first applied to him in the report of the battle of Slane in 947 in the Annals of Ulster.

Amlaíb Cuarán.question: It is from these references that _____örleifsson Kvaran and his siblings chose the name "Kvaran" as their own

Amlaíb Cuarán.question: Churches in Brega, including _____ and Dunleer, guarded by Amlaíb's soldiers, were a particular target of the raids
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: Churches in Brega, including Monasterboice and Dunleer, guarded by Amlaíb's soldiers, were a particular target of the raids.

Amlaíb Cuarán.subject: Environment & Ecology
Amlaíb Cuarán.question: A second invasion from the north in _____, this time an alliance including Máel Coluim's Scots and also Britons and Saxons, was defeated
Amlaíb Cuarán.fact: A second invasion from the north in 952, this time an alliance including Máel Coluim's Scots and also Britons and Saxons, was defeated. Amlaíb Cuarán.question: In 980 Máel _____ had the support of the Leinstermen when he faced Amlaíb's sons—Amlaíb himself was by now an old man—near the hill of Tara

Ammonitina.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ammonitina.question: The _____ was Extinct suborder of ammonites.
Ammonitina.fact: Ammonitina comprises a diverse suborder of ammonite cephalopods that lived during the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods of the Mesozoic Era. The shells of Ammonitina are typically planospiral, coiled in a single plane and symmetrical from side to side.

Ammonitina.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ammonitina.question: Lower Jurassic superfamilies include the _____, Eoceroceratoidea, and Hildoceratoidea, which is in part Middle Jurassic
Ammonitina.fact: Lower Jurassic superfamilies include the Psiloceratoidea, Eoceroceratoidea, and Hildoceratoidea, which is in part Middle Jurassic.

Ammonitina.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ammonitina.question: Superfamilies from the _____ and Upper Jurassic include the Stephanoceratoidea, Perisphinctoidea, and Haploceratoidea; the Perisphinctoidea and Haploceratoidea continued well into the Cretaceous
Ammonitina.fact: Lower Jurassic superfamilies include the Psiloceratoidea, Eoceroceratoidea, and Hildoceratoidea, which is in part Middle Jurassic. Superfamilies from the Middle and Upper Jurassic include the Stephanoceratoidea, Perisphinctoidea, and Haploceratoidea; the Perisphinctoidea and Haploceratoidea continued well into the Cretaceous.

Ammonitina.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ammonitina.question: Exclusively Cretaceous superfamilies include the _____, Hoplitoidea, and the Acanthoceratoidea
Ammonitina.fact: Exclusively Cretaceous superfamilies include the Desmoceratacea, Hoplitoidea, and the Acanthoceratoidea.

Ammonitina.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ammonitina.question: The Psiloceratoidea from the _____ stands alone
Ammonitina.fact: The Eoderoceratoidea of the Lower Jurassic gave rise in the middle of the epoch to the Hilderceratidae, which in turn gave rise early in the Middle Jurassic to the Stephanoceratoidea, Perisphinctoidea, and Haploceratoidea. The Psiloceratoidea from the Lower Jurassic stands alone.

Ammonitina.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ammonitina.question: The Cretaceous Desmoceratoidea are derived from the _____ separately from Jurassic forms and give rise to the Hoplitoidea and to the Acanthoceratoidea
Ammonitina.fact: The Cretaceous Desmoceratoidea are derived from the Phylloceratina separately from Jurassic forms and give rise to the Hoplitoidea and to the Acanthoceratoidea.
